verses.text: Remind people to submit to rulers and authorities, obey them, and be ready to do every good work.
They shouldn't slander anyone or be argumentative. They should be gentle and show consideration for everyone.
We too were once foolish, disobedient, and led astray. We were enslaved to all kinds of desires and pleasures. We lived with malice and envy, hating others and being hated.
But when God our Savior showed his kindness and love for humanity,
he saved us—not because of good things we had done, but because of his mercy. He saved us through the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit,
whom he generously poured out on us through Jesus Christ our Savior,
so that by his grace we could be made right and become heirs with the hope of eternal life.
This saying is trustworthy. I want you to insist on these things, so those who have believed God will be careful to devote themselves to good works. These things are good and helpful for everyone.
But avoid foolish arguments, family trees, quarrels, and disputes about the law. They're useless and pointless.
Warn a divisive person once, and then a second time. After that, have nothing more to do with them.
You know that such a person is twisted and keeps sinning, condemning themselves.
When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, do your best to come to me in Nicopolis, because I've decided to spend the winter there.
Help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way, and make sure they have everything they need.
Our people should learn to devote themselves to doing good, meeting urgent needs, so they won't live unproductive lives.
Everyone with me sends greetings. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
